title: The Horizon of Devil's Throat
premise: Desert ranger Ansel Okafor, who has measured his life in miles rather than years, is hired to find a vanished government survey team in the Devil's Throat badlands. The only trail leads to a wrecked airship carrying a sealed manifest the government will kill to bury, and Ansel must race a ruthless salvage fleet to it, beating them by six tides before the dry season seals the canyon forever. Alongside Ilsa Reyes, the survey team's sole survivor and the woman whose testimony could topple the officials who ordered the cover-up, Ansel discovers the thieves he has chased for twenty years were never criminals at all. In the end, Ansel chooses justice outside the law, burning the manifest's official copy while letting the truth loose among the desert people, and stays with Ilsa rather than returning to the badge that made him measure everything in distance.
about_author: Xanthe Kavanagh is the pen name of a former field cartographer who spent a decade mapping arid basins across three continents before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels where landscapes are characters and every mile costs something.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Ansel Okafor tracks a petty thief across the flats, reflecting on two decades of measuring life in distances instead of days. He catches the boy but lets him go, uneasy with what the badge demands. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: quiet restlessness — a man who has mastered the desert but lost track of himself.

chapters.title: The Survey That Vanished
chapters.summary: A government liaison hires Ansel to find a missing survey team; their camp stands intact, gear stacked neatly, no tracks leading out. Ansel finds one boot print that ends mid-stride and a scrap of survey film hidden under a stone. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into dread — this disappearance was engineered.

chapters.title: The Woman Under the Sand
chapters.summary: Ansel digs out Ilsa Reyes, half-buried and delirious, the survey team's junior cartographer and sole survivor. She raves about a wreck in the Throat and men with government papers shooting at her own team. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: terror and defiance — she woke up knowing too much to be allowed to live.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Ilsa reveals the team found a downed airship whose manifest implicates a minister in selling water rights; the 'salvage fleet' — government contractors — is already moving. The dry season closes the canyon in six tides. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: reluctant commitment — Ansel signs on not for duty but because the math of the lie offends him.

chapters.title: The Fleet on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Crossing the salt pans, they spot the salvage fleet's dust plume and realize the contractors are a day ahead. A night raid on an outpost yields fuel and a radio, but Ansel kills a man for the first time in years. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: moral corrosion begins — power over life and death sits easily in his hand again, and that frightens him.

chapters.title: What the Thief Knew
chapters.summary: The boy Ansel freed reappears as a guide through the slot canyons, revealing smugglers have used the Throat for years — and that the vanished survey team walked into an ambush meant for them. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: grief and resolve — her colleagues died as collateral, and she refuses to be collateral too.

chapters.title: Tide Against Tide
chapters.summary: A flash flood traps them in the narrows with two fleet scouts; Ansel saves one from drowning, learning the fleet's route and timetable — and that the minister plans to destroy the wreck with everyone near it. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: trust forged in water and fear — Ansel and Ilsa stop being employer and witness.

chapters.title: The Wreck of the Meridian Star
chapters.summary: They reach the airship hours ahead of the fleet and find the surviving survey leader alive inside, guarding the manifest — and willing to trade it back to the government for amnesty. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: betrayal — the man they raced to save would sell the truth to save himself.

chapters.title: Devil's Throat
chapters.summary: The fleet arrives; in the collapsing canyon, Ansel takes the manifest, Ilsa faces the survey leader, and the dry season's last tide seals the fleet's heavy equipment in silt. Ansel burns the official copy and scatters duplicates among the canyon settlements. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: climax — love declared in gunfire, duty abandoned mid-battle.

chapters.title: The Long Way Home
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the truth spreads town by town while the minister's investigation stalls without evidence. Ansel turns in his badge, measures nothing, and rides east with Ilsa toward a horizon that finally means something other than distance. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: resolution — a man who counted miles learns to count mornings.
